history.new: Published theorem - for every N there is a unique operation on {1..N} with p*1 = p+1 mod N and p*(q+1) = (p*q)*(p+1) for q < N (the recursion without its wrap-around instance), and it is left-distributive iff N is a power of 2 (R. Laver 1992/1995; elementary proof in A. Drapal's survey; see P. Dehornoy, Braids and Self-Distributivity (2000), Ch. X; P. Dehornoy, 'Some aspects of the SD-world', arXiv:1711.09792; P. Biane, arXiv:1810.00548). Lean checks A_3 and the non-existence for N = 3 (laver3_left_distributive, no_anchored_ld_three); the general theorem is not re-proved by the lab.

statement:
An anchored left-distributive magma (x*0 = x+1 mod N, x(yz) = (xy)(xz)) of size N exists exactly for
N = 1, 2, 4, 8 among N <= 10 and is then unique (the Laver table A_n); Laver's recursion yields
left-distributive tables exactly at the powers of 2 up to N = 64 (verified to N = 256 exhaustively).
title: Left-distributivity with a successor anchor: the Laver tables (rediscovery)
